_note: Focus areas for the AI-analysis dashboard. The 'analysis' text is an AI draft (Claude) from the plan's sourced facts, NOT reviewed and NOT computed from radar data. In the refined version this file is generated at build time from the pipeline outputs (AI writes text, code fills every number, a person reviews it; reports/AI integration in SAR prototype.md). scripts/make-focus-areas.mjs adds 'code' and 'center' from the DOSM districts.

kelantan.title: Most people evacuated
kelantan.tagline: River floodplain upstream of the delta

facts.text: On 29 Nov 2024 Pasir Mas had the most evacuees in Kelantan: 22,486.

drivers.text: Rain is the trigger: monsoon surges filled the Kelantan River, which drains most of the state.
Land use upstream adds runoff, but in river modelling, changes in rain had about 3–4 times the effect of land-use change. So we never say forest loss causes the floods.

kelantan.ai_focus: Measure where new water spread between the 17 Nov and 29 Nov passes, rank the villages it reached, and flag fields where the physics map and the AI second opinion disagree.
kelantan.ai_draft: Pasir Mas is the first place to check. It had the most evacuees on 29 Nov, and it sits on low land along the river. The radar map for this district is made at the event. Then this summary will say where new water spread, and how sure we are.

kelantan.title: Low delta by the sea

facts.text: On 29 Nov 2024 Tumpat had 11,105 evacuees, the second highest in Kelantan.

drivers.text: The coast is the bottleneck: flood risk rises when heavy rain meets high tides, which slow drainage of the flat delta.

kelantan.ai_focus: Track how long water stayed in the delta across all six passes, and compare it with Pasir Mas upstream to see whether the coast held the water back.
kelantan.ai_draft: Tumpat is where the river reaches the sea. Water here can stay longer when tides are high. The AI summary will compare the six radar passes to show if the delta drained more slowly than the land upstream.

kelantan.title: Where the river meets the sea
kelantan.tagline: State capital at the river mouth

facts.text: The Kelantan River basin covers about 12,000–13,000 km², more than 85% of the state, and overflows regularly from November to February.
On 1 Dec 2024, 97,128 people in Kelantan were affected, from 30,017 families.

drivers.text: Towns are hard for radar: flooded streets can look bright, not dark, so town pixels are marked unreliable.

kelantan.ai_focus: Separate open floodwater around the town from built-up areas, where radar is unreliable, so the summary never claims a street was dry or wet without evidence.
kelantan.ai_draft: Kota Bharu is a city at the river mouth. Radar sees floods in open fields well but struggles between buildings. The AI summary will report water around the town and mark the town centre as uncertain.

kedah.title: Heart of the rice bowl

facts.text: The MADA granary grows about 37% of Malaysia's rice.
Season 2/2026 covers 99,489 ha in three phases, starting 23 Sep, 3 Oct and 13 Oct.

drivers.text: People flood the fields on a schedule set by dam water and rain, before seeding.

kedah.ai_focus: Group every paddy field by how its HH and HV echoes change over the six NISAR dates (k-means, no labels), then report the share of fields in each stage: flooded, growing, or not rice.
kedah.ai_draft: Kota Setar has the most continuous paddy in our area. The AI will group fields by how their radar echo changed from 23 Sep to 19 Oct. Then this summary will say which fields filled first and how that fits MADA's three phases.

kedah.title: Northern paddy belt
kedah.tagline: About a third of our Kedah radar area

facts.text: Kubang Pasu covers about 31% of our Kedah radar area, the largest share of any district (our measurement from DOSM boundaries).
We found no MADA map of which blocks belong to which phase, so timing is checked against the whole schedule.

drivers.text: Irrigation this season depends on rain: dams stood at 35.76% on 17 Sep 2026.

kedah.ai_focus: Compare the date each field first turned dark with the three MADA phase windows, and list fields still dry after the last phase began.
kedah.ai_draft: Kubang Pasu is the biggest part of our Kedah view. The AI summary will compare when fields first held water with MADA's three start dates, and point out areas that were still dry after the last phase began.

kedah.title: Inland edge of the granary
kedah.tagline: Only partly inside our radar area

facts.text: About 63% of Pendang lies inside our radar area; the rest has no radar data in this prototype (our measurement).
By 13 Oct 2026 MADA dam storage had risen to 40.13%.

drivers.text: Smooth dry soil can look like water to radar, so a drought year raises the risk of false alarms.

kedah.ai_focus: Check fields that look wet on only one date against neighbouring dates, to separate real field water from smooth dry soil.
kedah.ai_draft: Pendang sits at the inland edge of the rice bowl, and part of it falls outside our radar view. The AI summary will check if fields that look wet stay wet on the next pass, to avoid mistaking dry soil for water.

items.name: Change detection
items.text: Same-track before and after: darker by more than 3 dB since 17 Nov (plan 04 §4.4).

items.name: Single-date water test
items.text: Otsu threshold on VV, capped at −15.5 dB (HydroSAR).

items.name: Town mask
items.text: Built-up pixels not detected as flood are marked unreliable (ESA WorldCover).

items.name: Slope mask
items.text: Ground steeper than 5% is never counted as flood (Copernicus DEM).

items.name: Normal water
items.text: Water at least 80% of the time in 1984–2021 is not new flood (EC JRC).

items.name: AI second opinion
items.text: A model trained on pre-event JRC labels, shown only where it disagrees with the physics map.

items.name: NASA water map
items.text: Consistency check against OPERA DSWx-S1, built from the same radar.

items.name: HH dark-water test
items.text: Smooth water in a field sends the flat echo away: HH turns dark (plan 04 §4.5).

items.name: HV dark-water test
items.text: HV must also be dark, which separates water from young plants.

items.name: AI field grouping
items.text: k-means on six dates of HH and HV, with no labels; groups named from radar physics.

items.name: NASA water map
items.text: Independent comparison with Sentinel-1 DSWx-S1, a different radar.

items.name: MADA schedule
items.text: First-flooded dates compared with the three phase start dates.
